experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffalos, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Observe some of Africa's largest elephant herds roaming freely against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its large elephant population and offers exceptional photography opportunities with iconic savannah landscapes and diverse birdlife including over 400 species.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa and home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. Guided bush walks and game drives allow intimate wildlife encounters including chimpanzee sanctuary visits. Conservation guides provide deep insights into wildlife protection efforts making this a uniquely educational experience.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Big Cat Safari
experiences.description: Explore the alkaline shores of Lake Nakuru, famously painted pink by thousands of flamingos. The national park also shelters white and black rhinos, leopards, lions, and Rothschild giraffes. A scenic drive around the lake offers breathtaking panoramic views from Baboon Cliff and Lion Hill lookout points.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Samburu National Reserve Unique Wildlife Drive
experiences.description: Discover rare and endemic species found nowhere else in Kenya including the reticulated giraffe, Grevy's zebra, Somali ostrich, and gerenuk antelope. The Ewaso Ng'iro River running through the reserve attracts dense wildlife concentrations and offers stunning landscapes of arid savannah, rocky outcrops, and doum palm forests.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange a budget shared shuttle or matatu (local bus) transfer toward Narok en route to Maasai Mara. The journey takes approximately 5–6 hours. Enjoy the scenic Rift Valley views along the way. Pack snacks and water for the road.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your Boutique Stay in Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation. Take a short walk around the camp perimeter at dusk to soak in the sounds of the African bush. Attend a brief orientation session offered by the camp staff about safety, wildlife, and the next day's activities.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or at the airport — grab a budget meal at a Nairobi airport café (approx. KES 500–800).
meals.lunch: Pack a simple roadside lunch or stop at a local 'nyama choma' roadside eatery along the Narok highway for grilled meat, ugali, and sukuma wiki (approx. KES 300–500).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the camp or a nearby budget lodge dining area — simple Kenyan staples like bean stew, rice, and chapati (approx. KES 600–900).

day_by_day.notes: Book your shared shuttle in advance from Nairobi to save costs. Carry KES cash as ATMs near the Mara are scarce. Dress in layers — evenings can be cool despite warm daytime temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive (6:00–9:30 AM) inside Maasai Mara National Reserve. This is prime wildlife viewing time. Look for lions, cheetahs, elephants, zebras, and wildebeest on the open savannah. July is the beginning of the Great Migration season — massive wildebeest herds may already be crossing from the Serengeti. Arrange a shared game drive vehicle through your camp to reduce costs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp for a late breakfast/brunch. Rest during the hottest part of the day (11:00 AM–2:00 PM). In the early afternoon, visit a local Maasai village (manyatta) near the reserve boundary for a cultural exchange — learn about Maasai traditions, beadwork, and daily life. Entrance fees are typically negotiated directly (approx. KES 500–1,000 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner walk or guided nature walk around the camp's perimeter with a Maasai guide at sunset. Spot smaller wildlife, birds, and enjoy the golden-hour savannah landscape. Return to camp before dark.

meals.breakfast: Early morning tea/coffee and light snacks before the game drive provided by the camp. Full breakfast on return (included or approx. KES 400–600).
meals.lunch: Simple packed lunch or camp-prepared meal — sandwiches, fruit, and juice (approx. KES 400–700).
meals.dinner: Camp communal dinner — traditional Kenyan stew, ugali, and vegetables around a campfire setting (approx. KES 700–1,000).

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-coloured clothing (khaki, olive, beige) for game drives. Bring binoculars, sunscreen, and a hat. Shared game drives are significantly cheaper than private ones — ask your camp to connect you with other guests.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day game drive starting at sunrise (6:00 AM). Focus on the Mara River area where wildebeest river crossings are most dramatic in July. Position your vehicle near a known crossing point and wait patiently — witnessing a crossing is one of Africa's greatest wildlife spectacles. Also watch for hippos, crocodiles, and large bird species along the riverbanks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive through the open plains. Look for the 'Big Five' — lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino (black rhino sightings are rare but possible). Have a bush picnic lunch prepared by your camp beside a scenic kopje (rocky outcrop).
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp by 6:30 PM. Relax, review your wildlife photos, and share stories with fellow travellers. Optional: attend a stargazing session — the Mara has minimal light pollution and the Milky Way is spectacular in July.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at camp before departure — bread, eggs, and tea (included or approx. KES 400).
meals.lunch: Packed bush picnic lunch — sandwiches, boiled eggs, fruit, and water (arranged by camp, approx. KES 500–800).
meals.dinner: Camp dinner — grilled chicken or fish with rice and salad (approx. KES 700–1,000).

day_by_day.notes: Full-day drives give the best value for your park entry fees (approx. KES 3,500–5,000 per person per day for non-residents — budget for this). Bring extra memory cards and batteries for your camera.

day_by_day.morning: Morning game drive focusing on predator activity (6:00–9:30 AM). Lions are most active at dawn — look for prides resting after a night hunt. Cheetahs are often spotted on termite mounds scanning for prey in the early morning light. Ask your driver-guide for known cheetah territory in the reserve.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning to camp, spend the afternoon on a self-guided nature walk in the camp's immediate surroundings (only in designated safe zones). Birdwatching is excellent — over 450 bird species inhabit the Mara ecosystem. Look for lilac-breasted rollers, secretary birds, and martial eagles. Alternatively, relax at camp and read or journal.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Talek or Sekenani gate village area for an evening stroll and to browse local Maasai craft markets. Purchase handmade beaded jewellery, shukas (blankets), and carved wooden souvenirs directly from artisans at fair prices. Bargaining respectfully is expected.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast — porridge, fruit, toast, and tea (approx. KES 400–600).
meals.lunch: Eat at a budget local eatery near the gate village — beans, rice, and chapati (approx. KES 250–400).
meals.dinner: Camp dinner or local lodge restaurant — nyama choma (grilled goat) with kachumbari salad and ugali (approx. KES 600–900).

day_by_day.notes: Never walk outside designated safe zones without a Maasai guide — wildlife roams freely outside the reserve boundaries too. Keep spending money in a money belt when visiting market areas.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hot air balloon safari over the Mara (optional splurge — approx. USD 450–500 per person, book in advance). This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience floating silently over migrating herds at sunrise. If this exceeds your budget, opt instead for an early morning game drive to the Mara Triangle — a less-visited section with excellent wildlife density.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mara Conservancies bordering the national reserve (such as Olare Motorogi or Naboisho). These community conservancies often have lower entry fees than the main park and offer excellent wildlife viewing with fewer vehicles. Arrange a guided walk with a Maasai ranger for an immersive on-foot wildlife experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for a rest. In the evening, engage with your Maasai camp staff — ask them to share traditional songs, dances, or stories around the fire. This cultural exchange is free and deeply memorable.

meals.breakfast: If doing balloon safari, a champagne bush breakfast is included post-flight. Otherwise, standard camp breakfast (approx. KES 400–600).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch in the conservancy or camp lunch on return (approx. KES 400–700).
meals.dinner: Camp dinner — vegetable curry, rice, and fresh fruit dessert (approx. KES 600–900).

day_by_day.notes: The balloon safari is expensive but can be shared cost-wise if booked as part of a group. Conservancy fees are often lower than national reserve fees and support local Maasai communities directly.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Mara Ecosystem's Oloololo Escarpment — a dramatic ridge on the western edge of the Mara offering sweeping panoramic views over the reserve and the Rift Valley. Arrange a guided drive with your camp. The escarpment is a great spot for landscape photography and spotting raptors riding thermal currents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Mara River for an afternoon hippo-watching session. The river supports one of Africa's largest hippo populations. Observe from a safe distance as pods of hippos wallow, yawn, and interact. Crocodiles basking on the banks are also a common sight. A knowledgeable guide will explain the ecosystem's dynamics.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at a scenic viewpoint — bring a thermos of tea or coffee from camp and watch the sunset paint the savannah in shades of orange and gold. Return to camp for dinner and a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast — eggs, toast, fruit, and tea (approx. KES 400–600).
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch by the Mara River — packed by camp (approx. KES 500–800).
meals.dinner: Camp dinner — lentil soup, chapati, and grilled vegetables (approx. KES 600–900).

day_by_day.notes: The Oloololo Escarpment road can be rough — confirm vehicle suitability with your camp. Maintain a safe distance of at least 10 metres from hippos on land, as they are highly aggressive.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated birdwatching morning walk (6:00–9:00 AM) with a local birding guide near wetland areas and the Mara River tributaries. The Mara is a birdwatcher's paradise — target species include the African fish eagle, grey crowned crane, saddle-billed stork, and numerous sunbird species. Bring a field guide or download a birding app.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recovery afternoon at camp. Use the time to sort and edit your wildlife photos, update your travel journal, or chat with fellow travellers. Alternatively, ask your camp if they offer an optional afternoon nature lecture or wildlife documentary screening.
day_by_day.evening: Night game drive (if offered by your camp or a local operator — approx. KES 1,500–2,500 per person). Spot nocturnal wildlife including leopards, hyenas, bush babies, civets, and genets using a red-filtered spotlight. This is a thrilling and unique experience rarely available in national parks but sometimes permitted in private conservancies.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-walk snack — banana and tea. Full breakfast on return (approx. KES 400–600).
meals.lunch: Camp lunch — rice, beans, and fresh vegetables (approx. KES 300–500).
meals.dinner: Camp dinner — beef stew with ugali and sukuma wiki (approx. KES 700–1,000).

day_by_day.notes: Night drives are typically only permitted in private conservancies, not inside the national reserve. Confirm availability and pricing with your camp in advance. Carry a fleece jacket — nights in the Mara can drop to 12–15°C.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning game drive in Maasai Mara (6:00–10:00 AM). Make the most of your last full day in the reserve. Return to favourite spots — the Mara River crossing points, lion pride territories, or cheetah hunting grounds. Take your time and simply absorb the raw beauty of the African savannah.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning to camp, pack and prepare for checkout. Spend the early afternoon exploring the Sekenani or Talek gate areas on foot. Visit a local community-run craft cooperative to purchase final souvenirs — your purchases directly support Maasai families. Look for hand-painted gourds, beaded sandals, and woven baskets.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at camp with fellow travellers and staff. Share highlights of the trip and exchange contacts. If your camp offers a traditional Maasai jumping dance (adumu) performance, this is a wonderful cultural send-off. Prepare bags for an early morning departure.

meals.breakfast: Early camp breakfast — porridge, eggs, and tea (approx. KES 400–600).
meals.lunch: Light camp lunch or snack before departure prep (approx. KES 300–500).
meals.dinner: Special farewell camp dinner — best of Kenyan cuisine including pilau rice, nyama choma, and mandazi dessert (approx. KES 800–1,200).

day_by_day.notes: Tip your camp staff, driver-guide, and Maasai cultural hosts generously — tipping is an important part of the local tourism economy. Approx. KES 500–1,000 per staff member per day is a respectful guideline.

day_by_day.morning: Early checkout from the Maasai Mara boutique stay. Board a shared shuttle or arrange a budget transfer back toward Nairobi (5–6 hours). Stop en route at the Great Rift Valley viewpoint near Naivasha for spectacular panoramic views of the escarpment and valley floor — one of Kenya's most iconic landscapes. Take photos and stretch your legs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Lake Naivasha en route to Nairobi (if time permits). This freshwater Rift Valley lake is home to hippos, fish eagles, and hundreds of bird species. Take a budget boat ride on the lake (approx. KES 500–800 per person) or walk along the lakeshore at Elsamere Conservation Centre — former home of Joy Adamson of 'Born Free' fame.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Nairobi by late afternoon. Check into a budget guesthouse or backpacker hostel in the Westlands or Kilimani area (approx. KES 1,500–3,000 per night). Freshen up and head out for a final Nairobi evening — explore the Carnivore Restaurant area or visit a lively local bar for Tusker beer and live music.

meals.breakfast: Early camp breakfast before departure (approx. KES 400–600).
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop at a local Kenyan restaurant near Naivasha — fish and chips or tilapia with ugali (approx. KES 400–700).
meals.dinner: Nairobi budget restaurant dinner — try Mama Oliech's or a local nyama choma spot for authentic Kenyan cuisine (approx. KES 600–1,000).

day_by_day.notes: Book your Nairobi budget accommodation in advance. The Rift Valley viewpoint stop is free and highly recommended. Lake Naivasha boat rides are best arranged directly with local fishermen at the lakeside for the lowest prices.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Nairobi National Park for a final wildlife fix (open 6:00 AM — the only national park in the world bordering a capital city). Entry fee is approx. KES 3,500 for non-residents. See lions, rhinos, giraffes, and zebras with the Nairobi skyline as a backdrop — a truly unique experience. Arrange a shared matatu or taxi to the park gate.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the park, visit the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage (open 11:00 AM–12:00 PM daily — free entry with donation). Watch baby elephants being fed and learn about Kenya's wildlife conservation efforts. Nearby, visit the Giraffe Centre (approx. KES 1,500 entry) to hand-feed endangered Rothschild's giraffes — a hands-on and memorable experience.
day_by_day.evening: Final afternoon shopping at Maasai Market (held at various Nairobi locations on rotating days — check schedule) for last-minute souvenirs at negotiable prices. Head to the airport for your departure flight. Reflect on an incredible 10-day Kenyan adventure filled with wildlife, culture, and natural wonders.

meals.breakfast: Budget guesthouse breakfast or a local café — mandazi, chai, and eggs (approx. KES 300–500).
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Giraffe Centre or a Westlands café — samosas, fruit juice, and a sandwich (approx. KES 400–700).
meals.dinner: Airport meal or final Nairobi dinner before departure — budget café at JKIA or a quick bite at a local eatery near the airport (approx. KES 500–900).

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and allow at least 3 hours for JKIA airport check-in and security. The Maasai Market schedule varies by day — check online before visiting. Keep some KES for airport departure taxes or last-minute expenses.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged transfer driver in the arrivals hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Nairobi to Maasai Mara National Reserve (approximately 5–6 hours by road, or 45 minutes by chartered bush flight if budget allows upgrade). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Great Rift Valley escarpment with stunning viewpoints along the way. Check in to your Boutique Stay in the Mara and receive a welcome orientation briefing from camp staff.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your accommodation and enjoy a relaxed sundowner drink on the camp veranda as the African sunset paints the savannah gold. Attend a brief introductory talk by your guide about what to expect over the coming days in the Mara ecosystem.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or at the airport — grab a light meal at a Nairobi airport café such as Java House (budget ~$10–15 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop at a clean mid-range Kenyan restaurant along the Narok highway — try nyama choma (grilled meat) with ugali (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the boutique camp's dining area — typically a set three-course bush dinner with soup, main course (grilled chicken or beef stew), and dessert, included or ~$25–35 USD

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your transfer arrangement in advance. If flying into the Mara airstrip, book the bush flight at least 2 weeks ahead. Carry USD cash for tips and small purchases as card facilities are limited in the Mara. Pack a light fleece — evenings in the Mara can drop to 15°C despite warm daytime temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive departing at 06:30 in the Maasai Mara National Reserve — the golden hours are the best time to spot predators. Look for lions, cheetahs, and leopards on the hunt. This is peak Great Migration season (July) so expect to see large herds of wildebeest and zebra moving across the plains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp for a hearty brunch, then rest during the midday heat. At around 15:00, head out for an afternoon game drive focusing on the Mara River crossings — one of the most dramatic wildlife spectacles on Earth as wildebeest brave crocodile-infested waters during the Great Migration.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp at dusk for the traditional bush sundowner. Enjoy a campfire under the stars with fellow travelers and your guide sharing stories of the day's sightings. Optional stargazing session — the Mara has minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast box from camp before the morning drive — typically fresh fruit, boiled eggs, a muffin, and thermos coffee (~included in stay or $8–12 USD)
meals.lunch: Full brunch back at camp — buffet-style spread including fresh salads, grilled meats, and local fruits (~included or $15–20 USD)
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at camp — roasted lamb or vegetable curry with chapati, followed by fruit crumble dessert (~$25–35 USD or included)

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, beige) for game drives. Bring binoculars, a camera with a zoom lens, sunscreen, and a hat. July is peak Great Migration month — Mara River crossings are most frequent between 10:00–12:00 and 15:00–17:00, so time your afternoon drive accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari experience — depart at 06:00 for an extended game drive covering the northern Mara Triangle, a prime crossing zone. Witness millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles in one of nature's greatest spectacles. Your guide will position the vehicle at the best vantage points along the Mara River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Picnic lunch in the bush prepared by camp — enjoy your meal in the wilderness surrounded by wildlife. Continue the afternoon drive exploring the open plains of the Mara ecosystem, searching for the Big Five (lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, rhino). The Mara is one of the few places where all five can be spotted in a single day.
day_by_day.evening: Optional cultural visit to a nearby authentic Maasai village (manyatta) — meet Maasai warriors, learn about their traditions, watch traditional jumping dances (adumu), and browse handcrafted beadwork jewelry. This is a genuine community-run experience supporting local livelihoods.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at camp — porridge, toast, eggs, and Kenyan chai tea (~included or $8 USD)
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch prepared by camp — sandwiches, fresh fruit, juice, and snacks eaten in the field (~included or $12–15 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at camp with a Maasai cultural theme — nyama choma (grilled goat), sukuma wiki (sautéed greens), and ugali, served around the campfire (~$25–30 USD or included)

day_by_day.notes: The Maasai village visit costs approximately $20–30 USD per person — negotiate respectfully and understand that fees go directly to the community. Bring small gifts if desired (not money for children — school supplies or books are appreciated). Stay hydrated throughout the full-day drive and apply sunscreen regularly.

day_by_day.morning: Guided bush walk departing at 07:00 — an armed Maasai ranger accompanies your small group on foot through the Mara ecosystem. Experience the bush from ground level: track animal footprints, learn about medicinal plants, identify bird species, and observe insects and smaller wildlife invisible from a vehicle. A completely different and intimate perspective of the savannah.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp for lunch and a midday rest. At 15:30, depart for a hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara (optional premium experience, approximately $450–500 USD per person — book in advance). Float silently above the plains at sunrise-level light, watching wildlife from above. Alternatively, enjoy a standard afternoon game drive focusing on the Mara's resident cheetah families.
day_by_day.evening: Champagne bush breakfast is traditionally served after the balloon landing (if you opted for the balloon). Otherwise, relax at camp with a sundowner cocktail. Evening campfire dinner with your guide recapping the week's wildlife highlights so far.

meals.breakfast: Full English-style bush breakfast at camp — eggs, bacon, sausages, toast, fresh juice, and coffee (~included or $12–15 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at camp — fresh salad, cold cuts, and fruit (~included or $10–15 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at camp — slow-cooked beef stew or grilled tilapia fish with rice and vegetables, followed by malva pudding dessert (~$25–35 USD or included)

day_by_day.notes: The hot air balloon experience must be booked at least 1–2 weeks in advance through your camp or a reputable operator like Governors' Balloon Safaris. It includes a champagne breakfast in the bush after landing. If skipping the balloon, the standard afternoon game drive is equally rewarding during the Migration season.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Maasai Mara early (07:00) and transfer to Lake Nakuru National Park (approximately 3.5–4 hours drive north via Narok town). The journey passes through the scenic Rift Valley floor with beautiful landscapes. Arrive at Lake Nakuru by mid-morning and check in to a mid-range lodge (e.g., Lake Nakuru Lodge or Sarova Lion Hill Game Lodge, approximately $120–180 USD per night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin your Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Big Cat Safari immediately after lunch. Explore the alkaline shores famously painted pink by thousands of lesser and greater flamingos. The park is also a rhino sanctuary — look for both black and white rhinos. The lake's surrounding acacia and euphorbia forest shelters lions, leopards, waterbucks, and baboons.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at a scenic lookout point within the park offering panoramic views over the pink-tinged lake and surrounding Rift Valley escarpment. Return to lodge for dinner and an early night to prepare for the next day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Mara camp before departure — light continental spread (~included or $10 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at lodge upon arrival at Lake Nakuru — buffet lunch with Kenyan and international options (~$15–20 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lake Nakuru Lodge — three-course set menu with soup, main (grilled chicken or beef), and dessert (~$25–35 USD or included in lodge rate)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru National Park entry fees are approximately $60 USD per person per day for non-residents — confirm current KWS (Kenya Wildlife Service) rates before travel. The flamingo numbers vary seasonally but July typically offers good sightings. Keep your camera ready throughout the drive as the flamingo spectacle is best photographed in afternoon light.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park starting at 06:30. Focus on the southern shores of the lake where flamingo concentrations are densest. The park is compact (188 sq km) making it easy to cover comprehensively. Look for the rare Rothschild's giraffe, colobus monkeys in the forest zone, and the park's impressive population of white rhinos.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, transfer from Lake Nakuru to Ol Pejeta Conservancy (approximately 2.5–3 hours drive north through Nakuru town and Nyahururu). Arrive at Ol Pejeta and check in to a mid-range tented camp or lodge (e.g., Sweetwaters Serena Camp, approximately $150–220 USD per night). Take a brief orientation drive within the conservancy in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the chimpanzee sanctuary at Ol Pejeta during the late afternoon feeding time (approximately 17:00) — the only place in Kenya where you can see rescued chimpanzees. Return to camp for dinner by the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge — eggs, cereals, fresh fruit, toast, and Kenyan tea (~included or $12 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Lake Nakuru lodge before departure — light meal of sandwiches and salad (~$12–15 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ol Pejeta camp — traditional Kenyan buffet with nyama choma, pilau rice, lentil stew, and fresh vegetables (~$25–35 USD or included)

day_by_day.notes: The chimpanzee sanctuary visit costs approximately $30–40 USD per person — proceeds support the Jane Goodall Institute's conservation work. Ol Pejeta conservancy fees are approximately $90 USD per person per day. Book your Sweetwaters Serena Camp well in advance as it is popular and often fully booked in July.

day_by_day.morning: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking experience — join a guided rhino tracking session on foot or by vehicle with a specialist ranger. Visit the Baraka Sanctuary to meet Sudan's legacy: observe the last two northern white rhinos (Najin and Fatu) in the world, protected 24/7 by armed rangers. This is an extraordinarily rare and moving wildlife encounter with profound conservation significance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full afternoon game drive across Ol Pejeta's diverse habitats — the conservancy supports the highest density of black rhinos in East Africa alongside lions, leopards, elephants, buffalos, and rare species like Jackson's hartebeest. Visit the Morani lion enclosure if any injured lions are in rehabilitation. The conservancy's open plains offer excellent big cat sightings.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a scenic spot within the conservancy overlooking the Ewaso Nyiro River, where elephants often come to drink at dusk. Return to camp for a candlelit dinner and a presentation by a conservancy ranger on Ol Pejeta's rhino conservation programs.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at camp — continental spread with fresh fruits, yogurt, eggs, and coffee (~included or $10–12 USD)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the field or back at camp — sandwiches, wraps, fresh juice, and snacks (~included or $12 USD)
meals.dinner: Special conservation dinner at camp — three-course meal with a portion of proceeds supporting rhino conservation (~$30–40 USD or included)

day_by_day.notes: The northern white rhino visit is one of the most profound wildlife experiences on Earth — approach with respect and silence. Photography is permitted but flash is not. The rhino tracking experience costs approximately $20–30 USD additional per person. Ol Pejeta also has excellent birding — bring your bird checklist.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Ol Pejeta at 07:00 and transfer to Amboseli National Park (approximately 5–6 hours drive south via Nairobi, or fly via Wilson Airport to Amboseli airstrip — approximately 45 minutes). Arrive by early afternoon. Check in to a mid-range lodge (e.g., Amboseli Sopa Lodge or Ol Tukai Lodge, approximately $150–200 USD per night) with iconic views of Mount Kilimanjaro.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin your Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views experience with an afternoon game drive. Amboseli is home to some of Africa's most studied and largest elephant herds. The park's open marshes and swamps provide perfect viewing conditions. On clear July afternoons, Kilimanjaro's snow-capped peak dominates the southern horizon — a truly iconic African scene.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at the lodge's elevated viewing deck watching elephants silhouetted against the setting sun with Kilimanjaro behind them — one of Africa's most photographed scenes. Evening dinner at the lodge with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Ol Pejeta camp before early departure (~included or $10 USD)
meals.lunch: If driving, stop at a mid-range restaurant in Nairobi (e.g., Carnivore Restaurant for a quick lunch, ~$20–25 USD) or grab a packed lunch for the road. If flying, light snack at Wilson Airport.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amboseli lodge — buffet dinner with international and Kenyan options, dessert station, and local wines or Tusker beer (~$30–40 USD or included)

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli National Park entry is approximately $60 USD per person per day. July mornings offer the clearest Kilimanjaro views — clouds typically build by afternoon. If self-driving to Amboseli, the road from Nairobi via Namanga is good tarmac. Hire a local guide at the gate for approximately $20–30 USD — their elephant family knowledge is invaluable.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise game drive departing at 06:00 for the best Kilimanjaro light and clearest mountain views. Amboseli's elephant families are most active in the early morning around the swamps. Look for the famous Amboseli super-tuskers — elephants with tusks so long they nearly touch the ground. Also watch for lions, cheetahs, and large herds of buffalo in the open plains.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a mid-morning brunch, visit the Amboseli Maasai Cultural Center for an authentic community experience — learn about Maasai pastoralist life, their coexistence with wildlife, and browse genuine handcrafted beadwork. At 15:00, take a final afternoon game drive focusing on the Enkongo Narok swamp where hundreds of elephants congregate to drink and bathe.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell to Amboseli — final sundowner overlooking the plains. Dinner at the lodge with a special Kenyan-themed menu. Pack your bags for the return journey to Nairobi the following morning. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day wildlife journey across Kenya's greatest ecosystems.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast box for the early drive — thermos coffee, fruit, muffins, and boiled eggs (~included or $8 USD)
meals.lunch: Brunch at lodge — full buffet spread with hot and cold options (~included or $15–20 USD)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at lodge — three-course Kenyan feast with traditional ugali, nyama choma, irio (mashed peas and potatoes), and Kenyan desserts (~$30–40 USD or included)

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is one of the best parks in Africa for elephant photography due to the open terrain and mountain backdrop. Bring a telephoto lens (300mm+) and a wide-angle lens for landscape shots. The Maasai Cultural Center visit costs approximately $15–25 USD per person. Tip your guide generously — $15–20 USD per day is standard for excellent service.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive at 06:00 for last elephant and Kilimanjaro sightings — a perfect farewell to Amboseli. Return to lodge by 08:30 for a full breakfast and checkout. Depart for Nairobi by 09:30 (approximately 4 hours drive or 45-minute flight). If time permits en route, stop at the Nairobi Giraffe Centre (Karen suburb) for a close encounter with endangered Rothschild's giraffes (~$15 USD entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Nairobi by early afternoon. If your departure flight is in the evening, explore the Karen Blixen Museum (from 'Out of Africa') or browse the Kazuri Beads workshop and fair-trade shop for authentic Kenyan souvenirs. Transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport with plenty of time before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Nairobi — carry wonderful memories of Kenya's extraordinary wildlife, landscapes, and people. End of a remarkable 10-day balanced safari journey.

meals.breakfast: Full final breakfast at Amboseli lodge — enjoy every last bite with a Kilimanjaro view (~included or $15 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Nairobi — visit Talisman Restaurant in Karen (mid-range, excellent menu, ~$20–30 USD) or Java House for a quick, reliable meal (~$10–15 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or pre-departure meal at Nairobi's Carnivore Restaurant if time allows (iconic Kenyan dining experience, ~$35–45 USD) — a legendary send-off meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security at JKIA. Declare any wildlife products at customs — purchasing ivory, certain skins, or protected plant products is illegal. Keep your KWS park receipts as souvenirs. Ensure you have your Yellow Fever vaccination certificate if required for your onward destination. Asante sana (thank you very much) — Kenya will stay with you forever.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffalos, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Observe some of Africa's largest elephant herds roaming freely against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its large elephant population and offers exceptional photography opportunities with iconic savannah landscapes and diverse birdlife including over 400 species.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa and home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. Guided bush walks and game drives allow intimate wildlife encounters including chimpanzee sanctuary visits. Conservation guides provide deep insights into wildlife protection efforts making this a uniquely educational experience.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Big Cat Safari
experiences.description: Explore the alkaline shores of Lake Nakuru, famously painted pink by thousands of flamingos. The national park also shelters white and black rhinos, leopards, lions, and Rothschild giraffes. A scenic drive around the lake offers breathtaking panoramic views from Baboon Cliff and Lion Hill lookout points.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Samburu National Reserve Unique Wildlife Drive
experiences.description: Discover rare and endemic species found nowhere else in Kenya including the reticulated giraffe, Grevy's zebra, Somali ostrich, and gerenuk antelope. The Ewaso Ng'iro River running through the reserve attracts dense wildlife concentrations and offers stunning landscapes of arid savannah, rocky outcrops, and doum palm forests.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Transfer from Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport via private luxury charter flight or premium road transfer to your boutique lodge in Maasai Mara National Reserve (approx. 5–6 hours by road or 45 minutes by charter flight). Settle into your suite and enjoy a welcome orientation with your personal safari guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the boutique lodge in Maasai Mara. Enjoy a private welcome ceremony, lodge tour, and champagne reception on the deck overlooking the savannah. Take a short, leisurely 'bush walk' with a naturalist guide around the lodge perimeter to begin acclimatizing to the landscape and spot resident birdlife.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the lodge's open-air terrace with panoramic views across the Mara plains. Attend a private briefing with your lead safari guide about the upcoming itinerary, Great Migration status, and wildlife activity zones. Enjoy a candlelit welcome dinner under the stars at the lodge's private boma.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at Nairobi airport — Crowne Plaza NBO Business Lounge or a la carte at a premium airport restaurant
meals.lunch: Light gourmet picnic hamper provided during transfer, curated by the lodge
meals.dinner: Private boma dinner at the lodge — multi-course Kenyan-inspired tasting menu featuring nyama choma, roasted root vegetables, and artisan desserts paired with South African wines

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private charter flight from Wilson Airport, Nairobi, for the quickest and most scenic arrival. Confirm luggage weight limits (typically 15 kg soft-sided bags for bush flights). Tipping envelopes and safari gear checklist provided at check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — depart at 06:00 in a private 4x4 Land Cruiser with pop-up roof. Head to the Mara River crossing points to witness the dramatic wildebeest and zebra crossings. July is peak migration season — expect massive herds, crocodile ambushes, and lion prides in action. Your expert guide will position the vehicle for optimal photography angles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Great Migration Safari into the afternoon. Enjoy a gourmet bush picnic lunch served tableside in the wild by lodge staff. Explore the open plains of the Mara Triangle, tracking lion prides, cheetahs, and large elephant herds. Visit a Maasai cultural village on the return for an authentic, respectful community interaction.
day_by_day.evening: Return to lodge by 18:30 for sundowner drinks. Hot outdoor shower and relaxation time. Dinner at the lodge's signature restaurant with a live Maasai cultural performance — warriors, song, and traditional dance around the fire.

meals.breakfast: Full English and continental breakfast buffet at the lodge — freshly baked breads, tropical fruits, eggs cooked to order, Kenyan AA coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush picnic — charcuterie, artisan sandwiches, fresh salads, chilled juices, and sparkling water served on linen in the bush
meals.dinner: Lodge signature restaurant — slow-braised Mara lamb shank, grilled tilapia with coconut sauce, and a Kenyan honey cake dessert with paired wines

day_by_day.notes: Depart no later than 06:00 for the best migration crossing activity. Bring a high-SPF sunscreen, wide-brimmed hat, and binoculars. July is peak season — river crossings can be unpredictable; patience is key. Lodge can arrange a professional wildlife photographer to accompany your vehicle.

day_by_day.morning: Hot Air Balloon Safari over the Maasai Mara at dawn — depart lodge at 05:30 for pre-flight briefing. Float silently above the golden savannah at sunrise, watching the Great Migration herds from above, spotting lions on kills, and enjoying a bird's-eye view of the Mara River. Approximately 60–90 minutes of flight time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-balloon champagne breakfast in the bush, traditionally served in the field after landing. Return to lodge for rest and spa treatment — choose from a traditional Maasai-inspired massage, hot stone therapy, or herbal body wrap at the lodge's luxury wellness tent. Optional: afternoon game drive to track the Big Five with your private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Guided night game drive departing at 19:00 — spot nocturnal predators including leopards, hyenas, civets, and bush babies using specialist red-filtered spotlights. Return by 21:00 for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast in the field post-balloon landing — smoked salmon, scrambled eggs, pastries, tropical fruits, and Moët & Chandon
meals.lunch: Light a la carte lunch at the lodge pool deck — grilled chicken salad, fresh avocado, and iced hibiscus tea
meals.dinner: Intimate candlelit dinner for two (or private table) at the lodge — pan-seared kudu loin, truffle mashed potatoes, and dark chocolate fondant with Amarula cream

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon must be booked well in advance — confirm reservation before departure from home. Weight restrictions may apply (typically under 100 kg per person). Balloon flights are weather-dependent and subject to pilot discretion. Dress in warm layers for the early morning flight.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Maasai Mara by private charter flight to Amboseli National Park (approx. 45-minute flight). Check in to a luxury tented camp with direct views of Mount Kilimanjaro. Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching experience immediately after settling in — head out with a specialist elephant researcher to observe and learn about individual elephant families roaming the Amboseli basin.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Amboseli Elephant Safari into the afternoon — follow large breeding herds across the iconic open floodplains with Kilimanjaro as a backdrop. This is one of Africa's finest wildlife photography settings. Visit the Observation Hill for panoramic 360-degree views over the swamps, herds, and the mountain. Guided by a senior Amboseli naturalist.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks on Observation Hill at golden hour — watch elephants silhouetted against Kilimanjaro at dusk, a bucket-list moment. Return to camp for a private dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at Maasai Mara lodge before charter flight departure
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at Amboseli luxury camp — grilled Nile perch, roasted sweet potato, and freshly pressed watermelon juice
meals.dinner: Private dining on your tent veranda — Amboseli camp chef serves a five-course menu including Kenyan lamb curry, saffron rice, and passion fruit panna cotta under Kilimanjaro starlight

day_by_day.notes: Pack soft-sided luggage only for charter flights (max 15 kg). Amboseli is dusty — bring a buff/neck gaiter and lens cloths for camera equipment. July offers excellent Kilimanjaro visibility in the mornings before afternoon cloud cover builds. Confirm elephant researcher availability in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Amboseli Elephant Watching and Big Five safari — early morning game drive departing at 06:00 across the Amboseli swamps and open grasslands. Focus on the famous large-tusked elephant bulls and family herds. Also seek out lions, cheetahs, and Cape buffalo in the open plains. The morning light on Kilimanjaro is extraordinary for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a Maasai community partnership village near Amboseli for a premium cultural immersion experience — meet community elders, participate in a beadwork session, and learn about traditional Maasai land stewardship and coexistence with wildlife. Return to camp for an afternoon rest, swim, and spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Bush dinner experience — camp staff set up a private dining table in a dry riverbed or open plain, with lanterns, white linen, and a private chef. Accompanied by a Maasai warrior escort. Stargazing session with a telescope provided by the camp astronomer.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at camp — eggs Benedict, smoked meats, tropical fruit platters, and freshly brewed Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the field — gourmet wraps, hummus, crudités, artisan cheeses, and chilled sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private bush dinner in the wild — wood-fired ribeye steak, grilled vegetables, roasted corn, and a Kenyan spiced chocolate tart with vanilla ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The Amboseli swamps attract the highest elephant density in the mornings and evenings — plan game drives accordingly. Maasai village visits should be arranged through the camp to ensure proceeds benefit the community directly. Bring Kenyan shillings for purchasing handcrafted beadwork souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Amboseli by private charter flight to Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Laikipia (approx. 1 hour). Check into a luxury conservancy lodge. Begin the Ol Pejeta Rhino Tracking experience — join a specialist rhino ranger on foot and by vehicle to track black rhinos through the bushland. Learn about the critically endangered northern white rhinos — the last two in existence — and the global conservation effort to save the subspecies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive behind-the-scenes visit to the northern white rhino enclosure with a senior rhino keeper and conservation scientist. Hear the story of Najin and Fatu, the last two females, and the IVF program attempting to save the species. Continue with a game drive targeting lions, leopards, and cheetahs — Ol Pejeta has one of Kenya's highest predator densities.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive along the Ewaso Nyiro River — watch hippos, crocodiles, and elephants at the water. Return to lodge for cocktails and a conservation-focused documentary screening, followed by dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Amboseli camp before departure
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at Ol Pejeta lodge — farm-to-table menu featuring conservancy-grown vegetables, grilled chicken, and freshly baked bread
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant dinner — slow-cooked Laikipia beef short rib, roasted root vegetables, and a local honey and macadamia nut tart paired with Kenyan craft beer or fine wine

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta is a working conservancy — revenue directly funds rhino and chimpanzee conservation. The northern white rhino visit is a once-in-a-lifetime experience; book the premium 'keeper for a day' add-on in advance. Walking rhino tracking requires moderate fitness and closed-toe shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Ol Pejeta Conservancy safari — morning game drive focusing on the Big Five and rare species. Ol Pejeta is the only place in East Africa with all of the Big Five plus chimpanzees. Visit the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary — a rehabilitation center for rescued chimps — for a guided educational tour with the primate care team.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided nature walk with a Maasai tracker and armed ranger through the conservancy's open grasslands and acacia woodlands. Learn to identify animal tracks, medicinal plants, and bird calls. Afternoon at leisure — enjoy the lodge's infinity pool, spa, or private veranda with binoculars for self-guided bird watching.
day_by_day.evening: Private sundowner experience on a hill overlooking the conservancy — gin and tonic with locally foraged botanicals, charcuterie board, and a personal butler. Return for a gala dinner at the lodge with a conservation fundraiser element — a portion of the evening's proceeds supports Ol Pejeta's rhino program.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast — avocado toast, poached eggs, smoked salmon, granola with local yogurt, and Kenyan chai
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch — grilled prawns, Caesar salad, and fresh tropical fruit sorbet
meals.dinner: Gala conservation dinner — five-course tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring locally sourced Laikipia lamb, wild mushroom risotto, and artisan Kenyan chocolate dessert

day_by_day.notes: The chimpanzee sanctuary visit is a highlight — chimps are most active in the morning feeding sessions. Confirm visiting hours in advance. The conservancy spans 90,000 acres — a full day is needed to explore it properly. Bring insect repellent for evening activities near the river.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Ol Pejeta by private charter or road transfer to Lake Nakuru National Park (approx. 2 hours by road). Check into a premium lodge with lake views. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Big Cat Safari immediately — drive along the alkaline lake shores to witness thousands of lesser and greater flamingos painting the water pink. Also look for white rhinos, which were successfully reintroduced here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Lake Nakuru safari — the park is renowned for its resident leopards in the yellow fever tree forests. Your guide will track a known leopard territory for a sighting. Also seek out lions, buffalos, and the large pelican colonies on the lake's southern shores. Visit the Baboon Cliff viewpoint for a panoramic aerial view of the entire lake and its flamingo-pink shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at Baboon Cliff or the lodge terrace overlooking the lake. Watch flamingos come in to roost at dusk. Return for dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Ol Pejeta lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch at the lakeside — smoked duck, artisan breads, fresh salads, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant — pan-seared Nile perch from Lake Victoria, sautéed greens, and a Kenyan cardamom crème brûlée with Rift Valley coffee

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru's flamingo numbers fluctuate with water levels and algae bloom cycles — July typically offers good concentrations. The park is compact and easily explored in a day. White rhino sightings near the southern shore are common. Bring telephoto lenses for flamingo photography across the water.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Lake Nakuru by private charter flight to Samburu National Reserve in northern Kenya (approx. 1 hour flight). Check into a luxury riverside camp on the banks of the Ewaso Nyiro River. Begin the Samburu Unique Wildlife Drive immediately — Samburu is home to the 'Samburu Special Five': reticulated giraffe, Grevy's zebra, Beisa oryx, Somali ostrich, and gerenuk. These species are found nowhere else in Kenya.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Samburu wildlife drive into the afternoon. The riverine forest along the Ewaso Nyiro harbors large crocodiles, elephants coming to drink, and leopards in the trees. Your specialist Samburu guide will share deep knowledge of the local elephant families — many of which are individually named and tracked. Optional: visit a traditional Samburu manyatta (homestead) for a premium cultural interaction.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks on a raised platform above the Ewaso Nyiro River — watch elephants and buffalo cross at dusk while hippos surface. Return to camp for a special riverside dinner under lantern light.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at Samburu camp — grilled chicken skewers, roasted sweet potato salad, and fresh mango lassi
meals.dinner: Riverside dinner at camp — slow-roasted Samburu goat, chapati, kachumbari salad, and a freshly churned vanilla ice cream with caramelized pineapple

day_by_day.notes: Samburu is drier and hotter than southern Kenya — pack light, breathable clothing and extra sunscreen. The Grevy's zebra and reticulated giraffe are photogenic and often approachable. The Ewaso Nyiro River is the lifeblood of the reserve — morning and evening drives along the river are the most productive for wildlife sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning game drive in Samburu departing at 06:00 — a last opportunity to find the Samburu Special Five and any remaining bucket-list sightings. Return to camp by 09:00 for a leisurely farewell breakfast. Pack, check out, and depart by private charter flight back to Nairobi (approx. 1 hour). Transfer to Nairobi city for a final luxury experience before onward international departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Nairobi. Check into the Hemingways Nairobi or The Norfolk Hotel (day-use room) for freshening up. Enjoy a farewell lunch at a top Nairobi restaurant. Optional: visit the Giraffe Centre for a final wildlife encounter — hand-feed endangered Rothschild's giraffes — or browse the Kazuri Bead Workshop for premium Kenyan handicraft souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Nairobi's finest restaurant — Talisman, Carnivore, or The Lord Erroll — before transferring to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for your onward international flight. End of an extraordinary 10-day Kenya luxury safari journey.

meals.breakfast: Samburu camp farewell breakfast — freshly baked pastries, tropical fruits, eggs any style, and a final cup of Kenyan single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Talisman Restaurant, Karen, Nairobi — innovative Afro-fusion cuisine, grilled tilapia, roasted vegetables, and a signature dessert
meals.dinner: Gala farewell dinner at The Lord Erroll, Runda — classic European and Kenyan fine dining, with a wine cellar selection, live piano music, and a send-off dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure at JKIA. Confirm all charter flights and transfers the evening before. Arrange for lodge staff to assist with packing fragile souvenirs. Consider purchasing a curated Kenyan coffee and tea gift set at the airport as a memento. Tipping guide: USD $10–15 per person per day for guides; USD $5–10 for camp staff per day.
